historical_record.description: Built about 1883. The bar's projecting metal sign, with neon lettering and a martini glass, dates from the years that made the building significant.
Built for Bernard Lagrave, a French immigrant from the Basses-Pyrénées, as a liquor saloon with living quarters above, near Railroad and Trinidad avenues, today's Third Street and Galvez Avenue.
After Bernard Lagrave died, ownership and running of the saloon passed to his widow, Catherine Lagrave.
The saloon was being run by Bernard P. Lagrave Jr., son of its founder.

Annie Pyle, a daughter of Bernard Lagrave who had owned and run the bar through the 1930s and 1940s, sold the building, then trading as Lagrave's Tavern, to Sam Jordan, ending about 75 years of Lagrave family ownership.

Sam Jordan spent six months renovating the building: new foundations went under all the exterior walls and new piers under the interior posts, and the old bar was stripped out and replaced with a cocktail lounge that had a horseshoe-shaped performance stage at the back of the ground floor.
The wooden plank sidewalk in front of the bar, a survival of the Butchertown era, was taken up and replaced with concrete.
Sam Jordan opened the bar as Sam Jordan's Tavern; it was soon known simply as "Sam's".
Sam Jordan announced his run for mayor of San Francisco, the first African American to do so, standing for the Freedom Now party; staff and regulars worked on the campaign from inside the bar.
A two-storey horizontal addition was built onto the rear of the building.

The bar began hosting a monthly Black Businessman's Lunch on the third Friday of each month, where African American business owners and people from the city's civic life met to talk over the issues of the day.

The Concerned Citizens Committee was started over drinks at the bar to put on a free community meal in Bayview-Hunters Point built entirely from donated food and labor; it was served each year in the week before Christmas for four years.
Sam Jordan went into semi-retirement and handed the running of the bar to his family.
Designated San Francisco Landmark No. 263, Sam Jordan's Bar.
The bar here is on the city's Legacy Business Registry.

unknowns: The city's African American context statement prints the address as 4004-4006 Third Street twice and as 404 3rd Street once.

notable_residents.name: Bernard Lagrave
notable_residents.detail: Bernard Lagrave, the saloon's builder and first owner, lived in the flat above it with his wife Catherine and their four children until his death in May 1888.

notable_residents.name: Sam Jordan
notable_residents.detail: Sam Jordan — longshoreman, Golden Gloves boxer, Bayview entrepreneur and the first African American to run for mayor of San Francisco — lived in the flat above the bar until his death in June 2003, and ran the bar until 1995.
